WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
“Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons: and they built David an house.” 2 Samuel 5:11
He sent his servants to Solomon at his anointing, “for Hiram was ever a lover of David”. 1 Kings 5:1
Hearing Solomon's request he said: “Blessed be the LORD this day, which hath given unto David a wise son over this great people.” 1 Kings 5:7
“There was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together.” 1 Kings 5:12
Of the twenty cities Solomon gave him: “What cities are these which thou hast given me, my brother?” 1 Kings 9:13
Chronicles' Huram, writing to Solomon: “Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, that made heaven and earth.” 2 Chronicles 2:12
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
He blessed Israel's God: “Blessed be the LORD this day, which hath given unto David a wise son.” 1 Kings 5:7
Chronicles: “Because the LORD hath loved his people, he hath made thee king over them.” 2 Chronicles 2:11
Cedar, carpenters and masons for David's house. 2 Samuel 5:11
Cedar and fir from Lebanon for Solomon's temple and house, and his builders working beside Solomon's. 1 Kings 5:10 1 Kings 5:18
A league with Solomon, paid in wheat and oil “year by year”. 1 Kings 5:11–12
Twenty cities of Galilee, which did not please him. 1 Kings 9:11–13
Joint fleets to Ophir and with the navy of Tharshish. 1 Kings 9:27 1 Kings 10:22
Solomon's levy of thirty thousand men worked in Lebanon “ten thousand a month by courses”. 1 Kings 5:13–14
Solomon asked for Hiram's hewers, “for thou knowest that there is not among us any that can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians”. 1 Kings 5:6

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not name Hiram's father.
Scripture gives no length of reign and does not tell how his reign ended.
No prophet in Scripture speaks to or about this Hiram; the “prince of Tyre” of Ezekiel 28 is a later king.
Scripture does not say what Hiram did with the twenty cities, beyond naming them Cabul.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textHiram king of Tyre, called Huram in Chronicles. Not Hiram the craftsman, “a widow’s son of the tribe of Naphtali”, whom Solomon fetched out of Tyre to cast the temple's brass (1 Kings 7:13–14); he has his own page. 1 Kings 7:13–14 2 Chronicles 2:3
Outside the BibleNot the “Hirummu (Hiram) of Tyre” who paid tribute to Tiglath-pileser III beside Menahem of Samaria, more than two centuries later.[7][21]
From the textThe page treats the Hiram of David's day and of Solomon's as one king, as Scripture's “Hiram was ever a lover of David” suggests; the question is shown with its holders. 1 Kings 5:1
